newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard surges on strong Q1 report.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard surges on strong Q1 report.

text.p: Shares in Hewlett-Packard Co surged in early trading on Wednesday after the computer maker reported fiscal first quarter results well above Wall Street expectations.

Several brokerage firms upgraded their ratings and earnings estimates on Hewlett-Packard after the company late Tuesday posted first quarter earnings of $0.87 a share, up from $0.75 a year ago. Wall Street's consensus forecast was for $0.75, according to First Call.
The stock was up 6-3/4 to 56-1/4 in New York Stock Exchange trading, topping the NYSE's actives list.

"Nearly all of the positive earnings surprise was driven by improved gross margins," analysts at NatWest Securities said in a report. They said gross margin improved to 35 percent versus 32.8 percent in the fourth quarter.

The NatWest analysts raised their fiscal 1997 estimate on Hewlett-Packard to $3.15 from $3.00 and fiscal 1998 to $3.65 from $3.50. They maintained their accumulate rating on the stock, which they said was "very attractive" at current levels and could reach $66 in 12 months.
Analysts at Morgan Stanley, Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette and Goldman Sachs upgraded their ratings on Hewlett-Packard and boosted their earnings estimates on the comapny.
